QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_28

question.text: Which of the following best describes 'High Water Mark' (HWM) in a Cat III AIF?

answer.text: The highest NAV (net of expenses and management fees) achieved by the fund, below which no incentive fees can be charged
Benchmark index value at the start of the fund life

explanation.text: The Logic: The High Water Mark (HWM) is the highest historical NAV (net of fees and expenses) the fund has reached. No incentive fee can be charged on NAV below the higher of the HWM or the reference hurdle. The Trap: Options A, B, and D draw on unrelated vocabulary (GST, leverage caps, benchmark index) and do not describe the HWM concept. Note: If the NAV has only declined since inception, the HWM defaults to the initial subscription price for incentive-fee purposes.
